thread:
Sara Nguyen: Heads up — Valencia Health reported a 3x p99 latency spike for inference yesterday after a config roll. Support attached a sample request id and asks for profiling / KV-cache hit/miss breakdown. Async is fine, but want a concrete plan. @Matt Cheng can you take the bench/profiling lead? :eyes:

Matt Cheng: On it. Can you drop the support request id + which model/seq distribution? I'll try a quick repro locally first.

Sara Nguyen: Request ID: val-req-2026-03-16-7b2f
Model: redwood-v1-13B-fp16, quant profile q2f16-07, typical seq lengths in their traffic: 256 (75%), 1024 (20%), 2048+ (5%). Support says spike correlated with a customer campaign (more long prompts).

Elaine Kozlov: I'll prep node-side probes. Need kernel-selector logs and the current batcher config. Suggest we enable quick KV instrumentation and do a small param sweep: --kv-probe=1 --kv-sample-rate=0.1. Also can run a sample flame with `py-spy` or `rbspy` during the window.

devops-bot: perf-bench triggered by @Matt Cheng for target set "valencia-spotcheck" at 2349991236. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/2349991236 (expires in 7d)

Matt Cheng: Quick repro notes: ran their prompt set against a dedicated shard. Observed p99 jump only when KV miss ratio > ~60% and avg_seq_len > 1024. Sample log snippet:
```
[2026-03-16T21:12:03Z] req=val-req-2026-03-16-7b2f seq=1500 kv_miss=true tokens=2048 latency=1.92s
[2026-03-16T21:12:04Z] req=val-req-2026-03-16-7b2f seq=64   kv_miss=false tokens=128  latency=0.12s
[2026-03-16T21:12:05Z] req=val-req-2026-03-16-7b2f seq=1800 kv_miss=true tokens=1800 latency=2.10s
```
Pattern looks like cache churn + longer seqs causing kernel fallback and higher latency.

Sara Nguyen: Good catch. Proposal: capture a targeted profiling run on a customer's shard during a quiet window, collect: KV hit/miss traces, kernel selector logs, perf samples, and model runtime metrics. I'm thinking 04:00–06:00 UTC tonight. Elaine, ok to schedule rolling probes then?

Elaine Kozlov: 04:00–06:00 UTC works. I'll: 1) enable `kv-probe=1` via feature flag on two canaries, 2) start async perf sampling on the target GPU, 3) export kernel selector trace at debug level, 4) add a temporary routing fallback to redwood-v1-6B if p99 > 1.5s. Will post runbook and commands before we start.

Support Liaison: I've told Valencia we'll do the profiling during that window and asked them to keep non-critical traffic paused. I've given them the expected timeline and that we'll share the artifact link and follow-up.

Matt Cheng: Implementation checklist for the run: 
- enable KV instrumentation: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/flags -d '{"kv-probe":1}'`
- start perf sampling: `tools/profiler/run_sample.sh --pid $RUNTIME_PID --out /tmp/val-flame.svg --duration 300`
- collect kernel traces: `journalctl -u kernel-selector -o cat --since "-10m" > /tmp/ks.trace`
- bench sweep: `tools/bench/kv_sweep.sh --model redwood-v1-13B-fp16 --seqs 64,256,1024,2048`

Sara Nguyen: Perfect. I'll own consolidation and the postmortem if we confirm root cause. Ping me in-thread if you need access to Valencia's logs or service account keys. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
